verdict: Credentials take an afternoon. Going live depends entirely on scopes: send-only needs a standard review, anything that reads mail triggers Google's strictest review plus a paid yearly security assessment.
start_now: If your agent reads email, submit for verification the day you know your scopes. The security assessment runs on Google's clock, not yours.

cases.case: Only your company's Google Workspace accounts (Internal app)
Read, modify or full mail access (restricted scopes)
cases.outcome: Verification + CASA security assessment, revalidated every year

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
Pick the smallest scope set for your features
steps.detail: Map each feature to one scope. Drop anything you don't call; one restricted scope pulls the whole app into the strict track.

steps.title: Configure the consent screen
steps.detail: App name, support email, logo, homepage, privacy policy URL, authorized domain. Internal vs External audience is chosen here.

steps.title: Create a Web OAuth client
steps.detail: Add your redirect URL (for Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, shown in Composio's dashboard). Copy client ID and secret.

steps.title: Test with up to 100 users while unverified
steps.detail: Unverified apps show a warning screen and are limited to 100 new users. Fine for building, not for launch.

steps.title: Draft the verification package
steps.detail: Scope justifications, demo video script, privacy policy checklist.

steps.title: Google reviews the app
steps.detail: Brand check, then scope review. Restricted scopes add a CASA assessment by a Google-approved lab.

blockers.text: Composio's Gmail form pre-selects https://mail.google.com/ (full mail access), a restricted scope. Keeping the default puts you on the hardest track.
gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose and gmail.metadata are all restricted. There is no 'light' way to read mail.
CASA assessment costs a few hundred to a few thousand dollars a year, from third-party estimates.
Scopes in your code must match the consent screen, or users keep seeing the unverified-app warning.
Exact review times for restricted scopes are not published by Google.

facts.q: Do you need a paid plan to create the OAuth app, or for any feature the agent needs (e.g. webhooks)?
facts.a: Restricted Gmail scopes need a yearly CASA security assessment by a third-party lab, which is paid (Google doesn't state the cost). Google's pages list no plan requirement for creating the OAuth client itself.

facts.q: Is there a sandbox or test environment, or do you test against a real account?
facts.a: No separate sandbox. While unverified, the app works with real Google accounts behind a warning screen, limited to 100 new users.

facts.q: Is there any review, approval or user cap before other people's accounts can connect?
facts.a: Yes. Unverified apps are capped at 100 new users. Sensitive scopes need app verification; restricted scopes add the CASA assessment. Internal (same-Workspace) apps are exempt.

facts.q: Which scopes cover what the agent must do, and does any of them trigger a review?
facts.a: gmail.send is sensitive (verification). gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted (verification + CASA).

facts.q: What redirect URL goes in when using Composio, and is localhost allowed while building?
facts.a: Use Composio's callback, https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Composio's dashboard shows the exact redirect URI for your auth config.

facts.q: How long do access tokens last, and how are they refreshed?
facts.a: Google doesn't state an exact access-token lifetime ("limited lifetimes"). Refresh tokens expire after 7 days while the app is in Testing with external users, and stop working after 6 months unused.

facts.q: Whose name do users see on the consent screen?
facts.a: With Composio's managed app: "Composio wants to access your account". With your own OAuth app: your app's name.

facts.q: If you switch from Composio's managed app to your own, do users have to reconnect?
facts.a: Not documented by Composio. Each toolkit has its own auth config; plan for users to reconnect, since tokens belong to the OAuth app that issued them.
